main.title: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
main.subtitle: A new journey through the forest of Niwen
main.summary: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a 2020 Metroidvania video game developed by Moon Studios and published by Xbox Game Studios.

cards.heading: Ori travels to Niwen
cards.text: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a 2020 Metroidvania video game developed by Moon Studios and published by Xbox Game Studios. Announced during E3 2017, the title is a direct sequel to 2015's Ori and the Blind Forest, and was released in March 2020 for Windows and Xbox One. A Nintendo Switch version was released in September 2020 by Iam8bit, and a version optimized for Xbox Series X/S was released as its launch title in November 2020. The game maintains narrative continuity with Blind Forest, and follows the journey of series' main character Ori in a new region called Niwen.

cards.heading: New combat and a change in visual construction
cards.text: The game was developed by Moon Studios, a studio based in Vienna with contributors worldwide. The game introduces new melee combat, and its visuals were given an overhaul from the two-dimensional artwork in Blind Forest, to the three-dimensional models played in multilayered backgrounds in Will of the Wisps.

cards.heading: Acclaim alongside technical problems
cards.text: Upon release, Ori and the Will of the Wisps received critical acclaim. Praise directed to the game included the story, characters, visuals, combat, elements of exploration, environments, chase sequences, and soundtrack. It is considered an example of art forms in the video game medium. However, criticism was aimed at technical issues such as frame rate issues and visual bugs, which were largely resolved with a day-one patch.

main.title: Animal Crossing: New Horizons
main.subtitle: The Deserted Island Becomes a Personal Project
main.summary: Animal Crossing: New Horizons builds an island routine from gathering materials, making objects and choosing who to share it with.

cards.heading: Begin with an island
cards.text: Animal Crossing: New Horizons arrived for Nintendo Switch on 20 March 2020. Tom Nook's island getaway begins with a modest camp rather than a finished town. The player gathers supplies, meets animal neighbours and gradually turns a shared patch of land into somewhere recognisably their own.

cards.heading: Make a place through small jobs
cards.text: Crafting gives branches, stones and other materials an immediate purpose. Furniture can be placed outdoors, so decorating extends beyond the walls of a house. Tasks such as fishing, collecting and making a tool sit beside decisions about where objects and buildings should stand. The island changes through repeated small contributions.

cards.heading: An invitation to return
cards.text: Time and seasons give those contributions a rhythm. Returning on another day can bring something different to find, while visits let other players see the place being made. The game provides activities but leaves room to choose their order. A collection, a carefully arranged garden or a conversation can become the reason for that day's visit.

cards.heading: The work of giving
cards.text: Added in the November 2020 winter update, Toy Day asks the player to move through the island and deliver presents. The celebration becomes a route between neighbours, rather than a single spectacle. Its pleasure lies in acknowledging familiar faces: the gift matters because somebody takes the time to bring it.

cards.heading: An artwork enters a virtual home
cards.text: In April 2020, Getty introduced an Animal Crossing art generator. It connected open-content collection images to custom patterns that players could bring into New Horizons. A painting could become a shirt, flag or object in a player-made gallery. The project joined a museum collection to tools people used to arrange their islands. It answered a question: how could someone encounter and rearrange museum art while spending time inside a game instead of visiting a building? The player's arrangement gave the collection another setting.

cards.heading: Use the tools people already share
cards.text: Getty built on the open-source Animal Crossing Pattern Tool and added collection searching and a converter for IIIF image records. Open-access material from other museums could enter the same process. Several kinds of work met here: collection images, a community-made tool and a museum team adapting the interface. Getty described the project as independent of Nintendo. An institution could contribute to a shared activity without having designed the game, using a tool to bring its collection into places that players were making.

cards.heading: A fish starts a conversation
cards.text: After its March 2020 closure, Monterey Bay Aquarium used game streams to reconnect with audiences. Staff Dana Allen-Greil and Emily Simpson later described how New Horizons? creatures prompted live discussions. Catching an ocean sunfish, for example, led to an extended conversation with viewers about the animal.

cards.heading: Keep ordinary experiences as evidence
cards.text: The National Videogame Museum's Animal Crossing Diaries call invited players to submit their experiences during COVID-19. It named both everyday routines and elaborate celebrations, and proposed combining contributions with interviews and articles. That collecting choice widened what could count as games history. A game was not only its release, rules or sales: it also held occasions that people wanted to remember. The invitation leaves room for different experiences rather than declaring a single story about lockdown. Preserving those accounts makes the people around the software part of the historical record.

main.title: Doom Eternal
main.summary: Doom Eternal is a 2020 first-person shooter game developed by id Software and published by Bethesda Softworks.

cards.heading: Hell on Earth
cards.text: Doom Eternal is a 2020 first-person shooter game developed by id Software and published by Bethesda Softworks. It is the sequel to Doom (2016). The story follows the Doom Slayer once again, on a mission to end Hell's consumption of Earth and foil the alien Maykrs' plans to exterminate humanity. Doom Eternal introduces several new weapons and enemy types, and has a large focus on resource management in which players recover ammunition with the chainsaw, armor by damaging burning enemies after using Flame Belch, and health with glory kills. Along with the single-player campaign, a multiplayer mode, Battlemode, was introduced. In this mode, players can either play as the Doom Slayer or as a demon, and fight until either the Doom Slayer defeats the demons, or vice versa.

cards.heading: A combat puzzle in motion
cards.text: Early production of the game began in 2017. A core development goal for Eternal was to address the shortcomings of the 2016 game, introduce more visual diversity and add more gameplay variety. Platforming segments, in particular, were introduced to break up the game's pacing and make the non-combat scenarios more engaging. The team described the game as a "fantasy combat puzzle", as players must choose the best tools to exploit specific enemy weaknesses. Unlike its predecessor, id Software developed the multiplayer component in-house to connect it to the single-player campaign. Mick Gordon composed the base-game score, however he had a conflict with id Software that led to both parties severing their relationship. Announced during E3 2018, Doom Eternal was released for PlayStation 4, Stadia, Windows, and Xbox One in March 2020, with a port for Nintendo Switch released in December 2020, and versions for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S released in June 2021.

cards.heading: Release, reception and The Ancient Gods
cards.text: Doom Eternal received positive reviews from critics, who praised its campaign, graphics, level design, soundtrack, and combat mechanics, though some disliked the increased focus on storytelling and its platforming sections. It was a commercial success, generating the highest opening weekend sales for the franchise to date. The Ancient Gods, a two-part standalone campaign DLC set after the events of the main game, was released between October 2020 and March 2021. Doom Eternal received five nominations at The Game Awards 2020, including Game of the Year and Best Action Game, as well as a nomination for Action Game of the Year at the 24th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards. A prequel, Doom: The Dark Ages, was released in 2025.

main.title: Half-Life: Alyx
main.subtitle: Half-Life Returns When the World Can Be Touched
main.summary: Half-Life: Alyx makes searching, aiming and handling objects into physical actions inside a virtual-reality resistance story.

cards.heading: Alyx before Half-Life 2
cards.text: Valve released Half-Life: Alyx on 23 March 2020. Set between Half-Life and Half-Life 2, it follows Alyx Vance and her father Eli as resistance forms under the Combine's occupation. Putting Alyx in the player's role changes the viewpoint without needing to continue directly from the series' last episode.

cards.heading: Search with your hands
cards.text: The virtual-reality design gives small objects and nearby surfaces more work to do. Shelves must be searched for supplies; tools operate alien interfaces; aiming can involve leaning around a wall. These actions place some of the tension in handling the environment, before an enemy has even reached the player.

cards.heading: Make room for different bodies
cards.text: Valve provided seated, standing and room-scale options, alongside teleport, shift and continuous movement. Those alternatives recognise that a virtual world is entered through a real room and a real body. Its included Source 2 tools also allowed community authors to construct further environments using the game's VR components.

cards.heading: Why Valve returned to Half-Life through VR
cards.text: Valve developed several VR prototypes, with three projects under development by 2017. They found the portal systems of their puzzle series Portal were disorienting in VR, but that the Half-Life systems were a natural fit. Walker said that Half-Life 3 had been a "terrifyingly daunting prospect", and the team saw VR as a way to return to the series. Additionally, they anticipated that fans would react negatively if Half-Life 3 were a VR-only game and felt a prequel carried less weight.

features.title: The person behind the viewpoint
features.summary: A virtual camera belongs to a body.

cards.heading: The room does not disappear
cards.text: Jed Ashforth's 2014 presentation on Project Morpheus lists differences between a virtual world and the body experiencing it. A chair and controller remain physically present. A represented sword has no matching weight, and a wall cannot supply the expected resistance. These are design conditions, not details automatically solved by a more convincing image. The presentation puts the player's expectations beside the sensations the equipment can actually provide. A world must accommodate that gap while inviting someone to believe they have entered its space.

cards.heading: Let the head remain yours
cards.text: Ashforth's instruction to preserve the player's control of their head follows from that changed viewpoint. Moving a camera for dramatic effect can conflict with someone looking around through a headset. His slides place comfort among the basic priorities of design rather than treating it as a finishing option. This is a historical presentation, not medical advice or a guarantee of comfort for everyone. It documents a shift in responsibility: framing an event now also means considering the movement of the person whose eyes provide the view.

cards.heading: A frame has a deadline
cards.text: Alex Vlachos's 2015 rendering presentation makes the technical side of that responsibility concrete. Its HTC Vive developer hardware runs at ninety refreshes per second, leaving about eleven milliseconds for each frame. The slides examine scheduling work around display timing and predicting the viewpoint. These are specifications and methods from that particular development period, not measurements of every headset. They show why smoothness belongs to the experience itself. A detailed room still has to reach the display at the right moment as the user continues to move.

cards.heading: A distant detail becomes reachable
cards.text: Tracking also changes what counts as a small visual effect. Vlachos warns that users can approach objects inside the tracked space, so an expensive detail cannot safely be treated as a permanently tiny item in a corner. Nearby floors and surfaces need attention too. A player who bends closer changes the production problem simply by looking. The design of a virtual place therefore includes the range of distances at which its materials remain convincing, alongside the frame timing needed to keep that moving observation coherent.

main.title: Final Fantasy VII Remake
main.summary: Final Fantasy VII Remake is a 2020 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 4.

cards.heading: Returning to Midgar
cards.text: Final Fantasy VII Remake is a 2020 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 4. It is the first in a trilogy of games remaking Final Fantasy VII (1997), originally released for the PlayStation. An enhanced version, Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, was released for PlayStation 5 and Windows in 2021, followed by ports for the Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S in 2026.

cards.heading: Cloud joins AVALANCHE
cards.text: Set in the dystopian cyberpunk metropolis of Midgar, players control the mercenary Cloud Strife. He joins AVALANCHE, an eco-terrorist group trying to stop the megacorporation Shinra from using the planet's life essence as an energy source. The gameplay combines real-time action with role-playing elements, an overhaul from the original turn-based combat.

cards.heading: Original creators return
cards.text: Final Fantasy VII Remake was announced in 2015 following years of speculation. Several key staff members from the original game returned, including Tetsuya Nomura as the director, Yoshinori Kitase as the producer, Kazushige Nojima as the writer, Motomu Toriyama as a co-director, and the composer Nobuo Uematsu. The staff redesigned the characters to balance realism and stylization.

cards.heading: Reception and the remake trilogy
cards.text: Final Fantasy VII Remake received positive reviews for its presentation, music and expanded story. Critics praised the strategic options in its battle system, while some objected to linear sections and repetitive side quests. It sold more than 3.5 million copies in three days and 8.7 million by March 2025. Final Fantasy VII Rebirth continued the remake project in 2024.

main.title: Gears Tactics
main.summary: Gears Tactics is a turn-based tactics video game developed by Splash Damage in conjunction with The Coalition and published by Xbox Game Studios.

cards.heading: A tactical prequel to Gears of War
cards.text: Gears Tactics is a turn-based tactics video game developed by Splash Damage in conjunction with The Coalition and published by Xbox Game Studios. It is a spin-off of the Gears of War franchise and a prequel to the first game. The game was released first for Windows on April 28, 2020 and subsequently for Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S on November 10, 2020.

cards.heading: Actions, cover and executions
cards.text: Each soldier has three actions to spend on moving, attacking or watching for an enemy to cross a firing line. Movement is free of a fixed grid, so finding cover and lining up a shot depend on the space around the squad. Executing a wounded enemy gives the other soldiers another action, turning a risky advance into a possible extension of the turn. Grenades close Emergence Holes before they release more Locust. Five classes and equipment modifications support different roles. Ordinary recruits can die permanently, making their growing abilities something the player must also protect.

cards.heading: Side missions and Veteran Mode
cards.text: In addition to the main campaign, players can complete different side-missions. At numerous points in the story, the player is required to complete one or more side missions to proceed. After the player finishes the campaign, Veteran Mode will be unlocked. It allows players to remix the campaign missions with different modifiers such as bonus damages and accuracy penalty. The game, however, does not have a multiplayer mode.

cards.heading: Sera after Emergence Day
cards.text: One year before the game, a subterranean race of creatures called the Locust Horde emerged on the surface and began a genocidal war against the humans of Sera. The sole surviving government, the Coalition of Ordered Governments (COG), fell back to the COG capital of Ephyra on the Jacinto Plateau where the Locust cannot dig through its granite bedrock. To prevent the Locust from invading the plateau and to deny them the spoils of war, COG leader - Chairman Richard Prescott (Liam O'Brien) - orders all major cities outside the plateau to be incinerated by the Hammer of Dawn (HOD), a satellite weapon of mass destruction capable of delivering laser strikes to the surface, in a scorched earth campaign. In addition, Prescott deployed a mop-up detachment in key-cities to eradicate the surviving Locust. In the city of Aldair, the mop-up crew of Alpha Squad is led by Sergeant Gabriel Diaz (Noshir Dalal), who had demoted himself to working in the motor pool after a traumatic battle in the Pendulum Wars.

cards.heading: The hunt for Ukkon
cards.text: Gabe Diaz and Sid Redburn recover intelligence naming Ukkon as the scientist behind the Locust's war creatures. Surviving a Hammer of Dawn strike does not end the danger: Ukkon destroys their base, and Prescott orders Diaz to kill him. The search for soldiers leads them towards civilian survivors and Doctor Mikayla Dorn, who knows more about their target. When she shoots Ukkon and he immediately heals, the mission becomes harder to understand. Diaz has orders to follow, but the information withheld by his own command may be as dangerous as the enemy ahead.

cards.heading: A trap in the desert
cards.text: Diaz relocates his entire squad into the Vasgari desert to teach them how to fight and prepare for the battle ahead. Alpha discovers an empty canister that Ukkon had used to inhale earlier, belonging to the Nedroma Health Institute - a quarantine zone and research facility for Rustlung, a respiratory condition caused by Imulsion exposure. Upon locating Ukkon's stash, they find the canisters are full of immune system boosters that only work against Rustlung, but with devastating side-effects. Realizing Ukkon is dying of Rustlung and in need of the canisters, Diaz prepares a trap to lure Ukkon by using the canisters as bait. Alpha successfully captures Ukkon, but reveals that he and Redburn have a history. Redburn knocks out Diaz and prepares to drive off with Ukkon back to Ephyra. Mikayla stops him, but Ukkon manages to break free and escape.

cards.heading: The secret of New Hope
cards.text: Diaz and Mikayla detain Redburn, against the will of Prescott who wants to execute him for treason. Redburn reveals he worked for a genetics lab called the New Hope when he was younger. Like Nedroma, they were trying to cure Rustlung. However, the scientists went mad and used genetic experimentation to evolve the patients into greater beings, but instead created the Locust. Most of the patients lost their minds and went feral, except for Ukkon - who had also developed immortality. When Prescott discovers that Alpha had learned the truth about New Hope, he attempts to kill them with the Hammer of Dawn to cut any loose ends. With Alpha presumed dead and no longer part of the COG, they decide to stick to their mission. Redburn reveals that the New Hope scientists created a fail-safe cytostatic gas that could neutralize Ukkon's healing ability. After they create the cytostatic gas grenade, Alpha proceeds to locate Ukkon's base of operations.
